Canofundeath.story: Newly promoted to the officer team, and already handed the loot council, which he has taken to with worrying enthusiasm. Frost death knight, never misses a raid, holds a firm opinion about everyone else's rotation. The thing to know before you whisper him about an item is that he carries a deep and unexplained grudge against balance druids, and the loot council is a very small room.

Ryzashaman.story: For the record, and he would like this on the record: three thousand two hundred and fifty-five Mythic+ rating this season, following certain remarks about whether he does keys at all. Restoration shaman, five tiers, keeps twenty people alive largely by putting a totem somewhere nobody is standing and then moving it. He runs on sarcasm and spite and has never pretended otherwise.

Phonchick.story: Solid resto druid. Watches the warrior stand in the acid, says nothing about it, and quietly undoes it, week after week, for four tiers. The only thing she ever asks for in the channel is an innervate, at intervals, into complete silence. Nobody has ever given her one. Put her in balance instead and she does respectable damage right up until something touches her.

Ázteco.story: There was a pull where the healers went down one after another and Ázteco held the whole thing together on her own for ninety seconds, shields going out faster than anything could break them. Afterwards she typed 'was that ok' and logged onto the alt. The officers keep one word next to her name in the notes and have never needed a second one. It is 'solid'.

Weeklynoleav.story: He puts the summoning stone up before anybody asks, every week, and calls it putting the wardrobe up. He puts the cookies out too. Tonight is the fifth time he has put the cookies out and the fifth time nobody has taken one, and he has told the channel so. On Sunday he will do it again, and the stone will be up before the invites go out.

Actualmoron.story: Preservation evoker. Twice a night he picks up a balance druid who is standing somewhere perfectly safe and sets them down somewhere with no floor under it, and he finds this funny every single time. He also, about once a tier, catches somebody already halfway off a platform who had no business surviving, and says nothing about it afterwards. Both of those are the same button.

Alysaar.story: Assassination rogue, top of the meter, and it is not close. Five tiers of it. She dies most weeks to something she has personally explained to two other people, gets straight back up, and is needed for the next pull before anyone can say anything to her about it. In lieu of flowers the family asks only that you stop standing in her poison.

Tubbygun.story: Dwarf hunter, eight tiers, has never missed an invite and has never once fed the pet. Welsh, and takes the England result personally every single time, in the channel, at length. Throws a punch at anybody who gives him an opening and does not hold back on the follow-up. A committed baiter, and by common agreement of everyone here, the master of it.

Prippin.story: He came here to blast. He is now on the council and takes the raid whenever nobody else will, and he has forgiven nobody for it. Shadow priest, an eighty on Nek'zali one week and single figures on the Explorers the next, and nobody has managed to account for the gap. He also does not care for the robot that wrote this, and has said so.

Katukas.story: Beast mastery hunter. Stands in melee. The pet waits out at range where the hunter should be and the hunter is in the middle of the pack where the pet should be, and that has been the arrangement for six tiers. Six tiers ago she pulled a boss early by accident and the raid killed it anyway. She has been chasing that from two yards ever since.

Hedstrong.story: Currently an arms warrior. Was something else entirely last tier and will be something else again by the next one, because he reads whatever the class discords are excited about and rerolls to it inside a week. Arrives at the front of the raid with the gear already sorted and a Mythic+ rating in the three and a half thousands, which he will mention. Nobody has learned to stop asking what he is playing.

Elelena.story: Four tiers in and the guild still calls him the new mage. He is an S tier frost mage and a D tier arcane one, and he has played arcane all season, because arcane is the meta and somebody has to. He has not complained about it once, which is somehow worse. Ask him about frost and watch his face do the complaining for him.

Rättfärdîg.story: Frosty. Protection paladin, and the best tank west of anywhere this guild has ever raided. Stands between twenty people and a stone golem four times her height for three hours a week without asking for credit, a thank you, or a mention in the channel afterwards. The only way anyone knows she has had a hard night is that she says nothing whatsoever about it.

Xenaphobia.story: Blood death knight, playing from South Africa on five hundred milliseconds of ping, which means he is tanking a fight the rest of us finished watching half a second ago. He drags everything within ten yards into one pile and reports that he is fine and has it. He has been right about that every time. Nobody has ever managed to check in time.

Cruzixl.story: Alfie takes the assignment nobody else wants, and leads the raid on the nights Norman is putting children to bed. Arcane mage, nine invites out of nine. What you notice first is the commentary. Every time he stands in something orange he says 'Alfie. Alfie, you' and then a word we are not printing, out loud, about himself, in the third person. He has never once done it about anybody else.

Friggjar.story: Holy paladin. Arrived this tier, said almost nothing, and started healing. Stands at the very back with her eyes on eight health bars at once, does not move for four minutes at a stretch, and dies about once a night to something she never saw, without mentioning it. She is on trial. The write-up is not going to take anybody very long.

Lymana.story: Vengeance demon hunter, two weeks in, and in her second week she held both golems for an entire pull and could not afterwards say how she had done it. 'There was a lot of green' is the whole account. She has asked the raid twice to stop standing behind the one that bleeds red. She is on trial, so she asked politely both times.

Dotjuice.story: Nobody can find any record of recruiting her. The trial invite went out and she was somehow already inside, imp out, standing on the mark. Two weeks in and nobody has seen her sign up late, or early, or at all. Demonology warlock, and a tidy one. The officers have her down as new and not one of them looks confident about it.

Grimsmonk.story: The nicest man in the Discord, and everybody here would tell you the same. Windwalker monk, polearm considerably taller than he is, straight through the middle of the pack. On Dimensius he sat the entire fight out on the bench and spent it saying something genuinely encouraging to every single person who did get the invite. He has not brought it up once since.

Findruid.story: S tier, and the best player in this guild by a margin the logs make embarrassing, four tiers running. When a pull has gone completely wrong and there is one person still upright with the boss at four percent, it is her, and everybody in that raid already knew it would be. She has never once brought any of this up. Ask her about it and she will start talking about your cooldowns, which she has also noticed.

Nórmán.story: The raid leader starts explaining the mechanic. Halfway through he goes quiet, because a child has got out of bed again and has to be walked back. He picks the sentence up where he left it. His connection is the worst in Europe and drops about one word in three, so nobody is ever sure which half they missed. When the channel talks over him he says 'right, that's it, you're muted', and the channel stops.

Pandemonium.story: Marksmanship hunter, and a good one. Turned up five tiers ago and nobody can remember formally inviting them since; they simply appear, at range, on time. Five tiers in that channel and not one unkind word about anybody. What they do instead is tell Phonchick she is doing a lovely job, whether or not anybody asked, roughly once a night.

Zindaz.story: Elemental shaman, first month with us. Assigned to the left side on his second pull, went right, and the boss died anyway. Nobody asked him to explain and he did not offer one. The officers have quietly decided to keep assigning him to the left side on the grounds that it appears to work. Nobody is certain who invited him either.

Andrewro.story: Subtlety Rogue. Duties: appearing behind the boss. Appearing behind the raid leader. Appearing in Discord ten seconds after the pull has already gone out to ask whether there is an invite going. Notable achievement: nobody in this guild has ever seen him walk anywhere, arrive at anything on foot, or still be standing where he was a moment ago. References available, though none of them are entirely sure where he went.

Arroul.story: WANTED, A BOSS: large, ideally stationary. Highmountain warrior, thirty-one nights, one axe, no questions. Will hit it until the situation resolves. Does not require the fight explained, though he will sit through the explanation out of politeness. Antlers included at no extra cost. Cannot be reasoned with once committed.

Billadin.story: On one of her first nights with us Billadin bubbled at eight percent, ran the sword back in and finished the boss on her own while the entire rest of the raid watched from the floor. There was a respectful silence. Then somebody asked how long she had been playing paladin. She said she wasn't completely sure, and that she had mostly been reading the tooltips as she went along.

Cmlsmall.story: BEAST MASTERY HUNTER (Orc). Range: everywhere, for years, without interruption. Habitat: the same spot on every fight, very slightly to the left. Diet: whatever the pet does not want. Distinguishing feature: quietly outranks most of the people who assume he is just some bloke with a bow. Behaviour when threatened: sends the pet. Behaviour when the guild is threatened: also sends the pet, then fixes whatever went wrong without mentioning it. Migration: none recorded, and none expected.

Elenski.story: In the age of the world-tree there stood a tauren who drank deeply before every pull, and the elders said this was unwise, and the tauren said it was a brewmaster thing. Three tiers he has held the line this way. The elders have stopped commenting. The keg is now considered part of the strategy.

Elfàrcher.story: Word is the nightborne turned up two tiers ago already knowing every fight, and has never once admitted it. Word is his bow is genuinely, on the tooltip, in writing, called P.O.W. x3, and that he has declined to explain this to officers, to friends, or to anyone who has ever worked up the nerve to ask. The prevailing theory in the channel is that he is a great deal better than he lets on and finds the whole thing funnier this way.

Kijosa.story: AVAILABLE: one haranir druid. Will bring starlight to your raid and a lantern to your problem, whatever the problem is, without being asked twice. Happy on either team, happy on any boss, visibly happier when somebody else gets the loot. Does not roll on things, which the loot has noticed and taken personally. Enquiries after nine in the evening server time; before that she is asleep and will not be moved.

Mousaios.story: Mousaios once held the raid together through an entire phase with a mace, a lantern and what he later described as 'a strong feeling'. Four tiers on, the troll still opens every night the same way: he checks everyone's health, decides it is fine, and then quietly moves three feet to the left where he can see them all.

Nanco.story: FROST DEATH KNIGHT (Blood elf). Habitat: melee, four tiers, thirty-four recorded nights. Plumage: two runeblades, permanently frosted. Behaviour: appears without warning at the boss's feet; will occasionally vanish and be replaced by a near-identical specimen answering to Nancometa, which the colony treats as the same animal. Call: silence, then a very cold noise.

Noint.story: Reports of the frost mage's death were filed early again. He stands further back than anybody has ever thought necessary, on the entirely reasonable grounds that nothing can reach him there, and is therefore killed roughly once a tier by the one thing that can. He is survived by an ice block he did not press in time, by several people who told him so at some length, and by himself, on the very next pull, standing further back.

Noughtilus.story: The tauren tanked five tiers under one name, then quietly rerolled, and half the guild spent a month asking who the new bloke was. He never corrected anyone. He just kept holding the boss where it needed holding, until somebody eventually noticed that the pulls had been going fine the whole time.

Rénstorm.story: One nightborne warlock. Steep in fel until the colour is wrong. Add a demon, unsupervised. Leave to reduce over six raid nights, stirring only to reapply. Do not open the lid to check on it — she will have moved the pot and it will be fine. Serves the whole raid, unless you were standing near her, in which case it does not.

Senrí.story: Holy Priest — seven tiers, one hundred and seventy-eight nights, four guild rosters, no gaps. Duties: healing; also remembering what happened in Aberrus, which nobody else can. Key achievement: outlasted every raid leader she has ever had. Reason for leaving previous tier: it ended.

Sesnä.story: The dwarf has fallen, shield first, exactly as he would have wanted. Twenty-eight nights across three tiers, every one of them spent between the raid and something considerably larger. Mourners are asked not to loot him, as he is only briefly dead and will want his hammer back.

Shabs.story: ELEMENTAL SHAMAN (Orc). Range: six tiers, a hundred and thirty-six nights, always the same three feet of floor. Feeding: lightning, mostly. Notable behaviour: does not chase keys, does not chase parses, does not chase anything — the boss comes to him, or it does not, and either way he is signed up for Wednesday.

Shamanbengt.story: Scattered appearances across seven tiers, tending towards brief but heavy. Twenty-eight nights recorded. When present, expect sustained storm activity and a shield in the wrong hand. Absence should not be read as a front moving out; she has a habit of arriving precisely when the forecast is worst.

Tröttpåmage.story: Bronze light over the whole raid, rising steadily. Six nights recorded, all of them measurably better for everyone else than they would otherwise have been. The dracthyr himself reports no change in personal conditions and cannot say why anyone is thanking him. Outlook: everyone's numbers go up and nobody knows whose fault it is.

Viamisolocky.story: Take one dark iron warlock. Apply curses liberally and walk away; they keep working without supervision, which is rather the point of him. Add green smoke until the tank can no longer be seen. Should the mixture separate he will reappear as a pandaren monk called Viamisosalty and punch things instead, and the guild has agreed not to ask which of the two is the real recipe. Serve either. Both work.

Zenafel.story: They still tell the one about the demon hunter who leapt blindfolded into a pack without checking what was in it, cleared the lot, and landed facing entirely the wrong way. They tell it because he did it again the following week, and the week after that, and is fully expected to do it again this Sunday. The healers no longer flinch. They have simply built the evening around him. He has never seen it coming, and has never yet been wrong.

Miists.story: Reliable on the monk. Spends most of the fight inside the green spinning circle doing the assignment and the damage at the same time, fists genuinely furious. Then every so often he brings the demon hunter out, and the raid is reminded why he plays a monk. He has tried it twice now. Both times somebody has quietly asked him to go and fetch the monk back.

Csipsz.story: New this tier. On his first night the paladin popped every cooldown he had on the opening pull, ran out of everything by thirty percent, and asked, in complete sincerity, whether that was 'about right'. Five nights later he is doing it again, and the boss is dying faster, so nobody has had the heart to answer.

Lilchain.story: SHAMAN, AVAILABLE. Five nights in and already on the sign-up sheet for the sixth. No armory, no Raider.IO page, no profile of any kind — the guild is fairly sure he exists because he keeps turning up and things keep dying. Enquiries in game only. He will not be answering the whisper; he will simply appear at the summon stone.

Luxyn.story: The young paladin, new to the herd, five nights old. Watch how he waits for the more experienced healers to commit before he moves — this is not timidity, it is learning. In a few tiers he will be the one they wait for. For now he holds the flank, quietly, and nothing on his side of the room has died yet.

Myoxtobig.story: Take one dark iron monk, aged eight tiers. Add mist, generously and continuously. Do not stir; he will circulate on his own. Season with a hundred and sixty-one nights of knowing exactly when the damage lands. Rest briefly between pulls. The dish improves the longer it has been in the guild, which is the whole trick of it.

Mîckê.story: HOLY PALADIN SEEKS PLACEMENT. Eight tiers, eighty-nine nights, one beacon, permanently on the wrong person for the first four seconds and the right one thereafter. Comes with a second character called Mickevoker, sold as seen. Will heal your raid. Will not heal the warrior who keeps doing that.

Dozakk.story: INCIDENT: Sunday, pull six. 1. Subject arrived four minutes after the invite went out. 2. Subject apologised, at length, unprompted, twice. 3. Subject was then the last one standing for eleven seconds of a fight nobody had expected to survive at all, surrounded by his own ghouls, doing his level best. FINDING: the lateness and the eleven seconds appear to be unrelated. RECOMMENDATION: keep inviting him. Send the invite earlier.

Pawnstaar.story: Interviewer: There is a paladin on the roster with your name on it. — Pawnstaar: There is. — Interviewer: People say that is where all your good gear went. — Pawnstaar: People are being generous. He is wearing what I found in a bin two expansions ago and he has never been invited to anything. — Interviewer: So the mage is the main. — Pawnstaar: The mage is the one who owns trousers.

Atrexy.story: The vulpera priest died as she lived: about four feet from where she was supposed to be, healing somebody who did not deserve it. Three tiers, eight nights, and a tail that has never once been still. Arrangements are informal. She has already respawned and is asking whether we are pulling again.

Atrexyen.story: They say the orc monk and the vulpera priest are the same person and have simply never been seen together. They say the staff is identical, which it is. Officers have looked into it, found that both were in the raid on the same night, and quietly closed the investigation without telling anyone what they concluded.

Firenze.story: Two nights, and the Discord is already convinced. They say the dark iron mage set fire to the tank on purpose. They say he has been playing since the beginning and only just decided to bother us. Neither has been confirmed. What is confirmed is that both nights went well and he said almost nothing on either.

Popmama.story: Popqa's paladin, and everybody knows it. She turns up for two nights at the end of a tier, when the roster is thin and the officers are making phone calls, brings a sword taller than she is, puts the boss down and goes again. The guild still talks about her in the past tense out of respect, while she is stood right there.

Popqa.story: Main tank last season, then vanished into a game with worse graphics and better fishing, and everybody assumed that was that. He is back at the front of the raid, tanking entirely on instinct, having never in his life watched a recording of anything he has done. He is also Popmama, Popka and Poppka, all of whom have been holding his spot.
